chunks: What al-Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sa'id ibn Janah, from some of our companions, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, who said:

I spent the night with al-Ridha (peace be upon him) at the foot of a mountain. When the end of the night came, he got up, moved aside, and went to an elevated spot; he urinated, performed wudu, and said:
"Part of a man's fiqh is to seek out a suitable place for his urination" — and he spread his trousers, stood upon them, and performed the night prayer.

key_terms.سَرَاوِيلَهُ: his trousers/lower garment, spread on the ground as a clean surface for prayer
key_terms.فِقْهِ: fiqh; here denoting practical religious wisdom and correct personal conduct, not merely legal theory
key_terms.يَرْتَادَ: to seek out, to scout for (a suitable place)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha (AS) teach about seeking a suitable place for urination as part of a man's fiqh before the night prayer?
ai.summary: Sulayman al-Ja'fari narrates that he spent the night with Imam 'Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (AS) at the foot of a mountain. At the end of the night, the Imam arose, moved to an elevated spot, urinated, performed wudu, and declared that seeking a proper place for urination is part of a man's fiqh; he then spread his trousers on the ground, stood upon them, and performed the night prayer. The hadith establishes both the etiquette of urination — seeking elevated ground to prevent splashback — and the use of one's garment as a clean, elevated surface for salat al-layl.
